status: Both first-seed complete native100ps protein panels and full-path, temporal-order and amplitude-bin analyses completed
training: Same architecture, initialization RNG, exact2048-example sequence,52,958,960 atom-query exposure and optimizer recipe; all weights random then trained. No static pretraining yet.
paired_array_definition: Mean,95percent paired system-bootstrap lower,upper; marginal exploratory intervals without multiplicity correction. All listed errors lower-is-better; raw amplitude ratios above instead have ideal value1.

resources.interpretation: Evaluation wallclock includes scoring/IO; same A100 model and per-panel NFE, not measured equal FLOPs. Actual inference ran on distinct GPUs while other authorized work ran concurrently.

complete_path_followup.interpretation: Both A/B improve all four measured CA position, increment, pair-distance and pair-distance-increment fair path scores over released PVB in this native-input protocol. Preserve this favorable evidence despite their all-atom geometry deficits. Versus h/v, A path-score intervals all cross zero; B improves pair-distance paths but other intervals cross zero. A/B differ clearly only on CA increment paths among these four endpoints. Two-draw CA path scores do not establish correct all-atom joint dynamics.

temporal_order_followup.definition: One minus chronological lagged squared distance divided by exact frame-permutation expectation, after shared protein alignment. Positive means adjacency advantage; not universally larger-is-better. No new neural calls.
temporal_order_followup.interpretation: Both coordinate models still show very weak adjacent-frame ordering compared with MD, despite nonzero RMSF and some favorable path scores. PVB overstates this lag1 ordering relative to MD and is not ground truth. Near-zero ordering is compatible with exchangeability, not proof of independent frames. Static pretraining alone cannot be assumed to repair this temporal deficit.

motion_amplitude_followup.bins: Evaluation-only true future displacement from last observation;44 low,26 medium,26 high conditions. Systems can have anchors in different bins; bins are not disjoint system cohorts.
motion_amplitude_followup.interpretation: Both suppress finite-window RMSF in the high-motion bin on average; B's better MSD does not mean it preserves larger fluctuation amplitudes. B has worse bonds/clashes than A in every bin and worse RMSF profile in the high bin. Do not label A intrinsically small-motion or B intrinsically large-motion. All96 conditions remain included, with TRAIN-frozen bins.

fixed_history_clock80_100.coverage: 48 systems,96 matched observed histories, two draws at each spacing for each model; original complete native80/native100 caches, no new neural calls for analysis
fixed_history_clock80_100.metric: Response of observed-contact CA pair-distance displacement and fluctuation observables to80ps versus100ps query spacing. Protein80ps lies below protein TRAIN100/200/400ps spacing, although80ps occurs in complex TRAIN.
fixed_history_clock80_100.interpretation: Both recipes reduce errors relative to h/v and show the correct sign in the mean response. However their displacement-response advantage over a zero-response predictor remains unresolved; fluctuation-response advantage is small but its interval excludes zero. A/B error differences are unresolved. Do not label smaller clock-to-seed response ratios as automatically good or bad, demand deterministic predictions match MD fixed-index differences, or claim time sensitivity solved.

answers_so_far: A improves several geometry metrics and MSD/torsion-increment errors over historical h/v on this panel, with unresolved RMSF difference. This is positive joint evidence on some endpoints, not yet full trajectory quality or the whole goal.

B improves geometry/MSD over h/v but worsens residue RMSF/torsion increments. A is better than B on geometry/RMSF/torsion increments here, while B is better on MSD. Similar mean amplitudes cannot establish matching motion distributions.
Neither reaches released PVB geometry. A has lower residue RMSF error than PVB but worse MSD; unresolved scores do not establish equivalence.

These A/B differences occur without static pretraining or extra optimizer exposure. Comparisons with h/v remain confounded by architecture/pretraining/resources and do not isolate the sampled-state hypothesis.

One seed, one time grid and protein-only results do not settle noise-regime, large-motion, complex or long-time performance. Keep both unchanged arms, second seeds, fixed-noise diagnostic and planned complete evaluations.
